item.title: Go Daily Question 20250517
item.description:
How many syntax issues are there in the following code, and what are they?

package main
import (
    "fmt"
)
func main() {
    var x string = nil
    if x == nil {
        x = "default"
    }
    fmt.Println(x)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
./prog.go:8:17: cannot use nil as string value in variable declaration
./prog.go:9:10: invalid operation: x == nil (mismatched types string and untyped nil)

var x string = nil Error

In Go, the zero value for a string type is an empty string "", not nil. nil is typically used for types like pointers, slices, maps, channels, and interfaces. Therefore, assigning nil to a string type variable x will result in a compilation error.

item.title: Go Daily Question 127
item.description:
What is the output of the following code and why?

func hello() []string {  
    return nil
}

func main() {  
    h := hello
    if h == nil {
        fmt.Println("nil")
    } else {
        fmt.Println("not nil")
    }
}
  • A. nil
  • B. not nil
  • C. compilation error
🔑 Answer Analysis:

B

hello is a Function value. Functions are first-class citizens in Go. Therefore, if h == nil is valid. Since function values have a value (an address), they are also not nil. Functions are also values. They can be passed around like other values. Function values can be used as function arguments and return values.

item.title: Go Daily Question 123
item.description:
What does the following code print, and why?

package main

import (
    "fmt"
)

type People interface {
    Show()
}

type Student struct{}

func (stu *Student) Show() {

}

func live() People {
    var stu *Student
    return stu
}

func main() {
    if live() == nil {
        fmt.Println("AAAAAAA")
    } else {
        fmt.Println("BBBBBBB")
    }
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: BBBBBBB Simply put, an interface variable has two values: one is its type, and the other is its value. For an if interface, the live() == nil condition is true only when both the value and the type are zero values.

item.title: Go Daily Question 088
item.description:
What is the output of the following code:

package main

func main() {
  var x *struct {
    s [][32]byte
  }
  
  println(len(x.s[99]))
}

A: Runtime panic; B: 32; C: Compile error; D: 0

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: B

  • The return result is always an int;
  • The return result can sometimes be a constant;
  • Sometimes function parameters are not evaluated, meaning the return value is determined at compile time;

Here, len(x.s[99]) Since the slice type of s is [][32]byte, len(x.s[99]) = 32.

item.title: Go Daily Question 078
item.description:
What is the difference between the following two slice declarations? Which one is more preferable?

A. var a []int
B. a := []int{}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

A: Declares []int uninitialized, pointing to nil. B: Declares []int initialized, pointing to an empty array.

A can be declared globally. B can only be declared inside a function.

A and B theoretically occupy the same memory space. Note: An empty slice points to a fixed address, so no actual memory is allocated.

        fmt.Println("nil")
        return
    }

item.title: Go Daily Question 040
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type person struct {  
    name string
}

func main() {  
    var m map[person]int
    p := person{"mike"}
    fmt.Println(m[p])
}

A.0 B.1 C.Compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: A 0

m is a map, and its value is nil. Getting a value from a nil map will not cause an error; instead, it returns the corresponding zero value. Here, the value is of type int, so it returns 0.

item.title: Go Daily Question 035
item.description:
What is the output of the following code and why?

func hello() []string {  
    return nil
}

func main() {  
    h := hello
    if h == nil {
        fmt.Println("nil")
    } else {
        fmt.Println("not nil")
    }
}

A. nil B. not nil C. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

B. In this problem, the function hello is assigned to variable h, rather than the return value of the function (i.e., it’s not a function call). Therefore, the output is not nil. Note that functions are first-class citizens in Go.

item.title: Go Daily Question 029
item.description:
Which of the following assignments is correct?

A. var x = nil B. var x interface{} = nil C. var x string = nil D. var x error = nil

🔑 Answer Analysis:

BD. This question tests the knowledge of nil. nil can only be assigned to pointers.

A: Type not specified. B: Empty interface can be assigned nil. C: A string is essentially a read-only slice and cannot be assigned nil. D: error is essentially an interface type and can be assigned nil.
